C3: The second segment (18:59–19:08, +4.78 km) was never proposed or agreed to in advance: the driver's own statement says the second turn-off was his GPS rerouting, and there is no rider message consenting to that segment before its 18:59 start. [F10 F9 F4] [RD-5]

[F11 F12 F13 F4] [RD-4]

C6: No waiting-time refund arises from the on-trip detour, since the billed waiting fee is $0.00 and metered waiting units are chargeable under the meter rules. [F7] [RD-3 RD-2]

The GPS record shows two distinct off-route segments — 18:40–18:45 (+3.17 km, up to 1337 m off route) and 18:59–19:08 (+4.78 km, up to 1687 m off route) — each of which must be reviewed separately under RD-1 [F3][F4][RD-1].

Segment F3 is exempt: the driver named a specific corridor before leaving the optimal route ("ok if I go round via Kranji Expressway?" at 18:37) and the rider agreed at 18:38, i.e. before the 18:40 segment start [F8][F9][F3][RD-5]. Consent covers the route the driver actually named, and nothing in the record shows the 18:40–18:45 driving plainly went somewhere other than the Kranji corridor; the BKE stretch being replaced was also documented as congested, at 40–49 km/h [F11][F8][RD-5]. The rider's own brief concedes this segment, and the trace shows no qualifying RD-4(a) incident or RD-3 stop request for it [F13][F3][RD-4][RD-3].

Segment F4 is not exempt. The driver's 18:37 request and the rider's 18:38 "Sure, go ahead" predate only the first segment; no chat message between 18:38 and the 18:59 start proposes or agrees to this second turn-off [F8][F9][F4][RD-5]. The driver's statement that the second turn-off was "his GPS rerouting" is a mere statement and cannot extend the consent to a corridor he never named, and it is in any case overridden by the system GPS record of the deviation itself [F10][F4][RD-5][RD-1]. No reasonable-cause exemption rescues it: the only traffic records are speed bands on BKE (band 5, 40–49 km/h) and PIE (band 4, 30–39 km/h), band evidence alone does not exempt under RD-4(b), and there were no incidents recorded near the route during the trip window [F11][F12][F13][F4][RD-4].

Only the unexempted segment F4 therefore enters the RD-2 refund: 4.78 km × $1.41/km = $6.74, the rate being distance fare $40.96 ÷ 29.1 km = $1.41/km [F4][F7][RD-2]. The lump fare figure of $11.96 for 8.5 km cannot be used, because it includes the exempt 3.17 km of consented mileage [F5][F1][RD-2]. No waiting charge arises: the billed waiting fee is $0.00 [F7][RD-3]. The RD-6 account flag is not engaged, since the driver's profile shows one upheld dispute with a route count of 0, so this case is not a repeated route violation [F16][RD-6].

claims.assertion: The trip contains two distinct off-route segments: segment 18:40–18:45 added 3.17 km (3.31 km driven vs 0.14 km on the optimal route) and segment 18:59–19:08 added 4.78 km (5.77 km vs 0.98 km). Each is a separate deviation to be reviewed individually.

The rider's consent at 18:38 ('Sure, go ahead') answered only the driver's 18:37 request to go round via Kranji Expressway; it was given before the first deviation and therefore can cover at most the first segment, not the later one.

The second segment (18:59–19:08, +4.78 km) was never proposed or agreed to in advance: the driver's own statement says the second turn-off was his GPS rerouting, and there is no rider message consenting to that segment before its 18:59 start.

No reasonable-cause exemption applies to the second segment: the only traffic records are speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) on BKE and band 4 (30–39 km/h) on PIE, and there were no traffic incidents near the route during the trip window; no incident evidence justifies the 18:59–19:08 detour.

This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so the unexempted extra mileage on the second segment enters the metered fare and is refundable: 4.78 km × $1.41/km = $6.74 (the per-km rate being distance fare $40.96 ÷ distance 29.1 km).
No waiting-time refund arises from the on-trip detour, since the billed waiting fee is $0.00 and metered waiting units are chargeable under the meter rules.
The driver has 1 upheld dispute in 90 days in the profile history, so this established deviation should additionally be recorded for account review under the repeated-violation rule.

weaknesses: The first segment (+3.17 km, F3) is largely excused by the rider's own 18:38 consent (F9) to the 18:37 Kranji Expressway reroute (F8), so we concede that portion and claim only the later segment.

The driver argues his GPS rerouted him (F10) — a plausible-sounding justification, though under RD-4 it fails because the traffic records (F11, F12, F13) show no incident and only moderate congestion.

Excess distance billed in the fare facts is a single lump figure of $11.96 for 8.5 km (F5); the judge may prefer the fare figure over our segment-based $6.74 computation, and the fare total (F7) does not itemise per-segment mileage.

claims.assertion: The first off-route segment (18:40–18:45, +3.17 km, F3) is covered by the rider's prior agreement: the driver proposed the Kranji Expressway reroute at 18:37 and the rider replied 'Sure, go ahead' at 18:38, i.e. before the segment started, so under RD-5 that segment is not a deviation and attracts no refund.

Only the second off-route segment (18:59–19:08, +4.78 km, F4) is a candidate unexempted deviation, since the driver's chat agreement covers only the Kranji Expressway jam-avoidance and not this later turn-off; the driver's own statement that it was a GPS reroute (F10) is not enough, as the chat record shows no pre-departure notice or consent for that segment.

The jam the driver described is real and documented: Bukit Timah Expressway was at speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) throughout 18:22–19:19 (F11), confirming the rider's own concession that a reroute around the jam near the start was justified, and no complaint of overcharging arises from the first segment.

No incident-based justification is available for either segment: the traffic records show no incidents near the route during the trip window (F13) and only band 4–5 speeds on the expressways (F11, F12), so the driver cannot claim the RD-4 (a) exemption and must accept RD-2 treatment for the unexempted segment.

This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (total $57.73 metered: base $3.90, distance $40.96 for 29.1 km = $1.41/km, time $11.40, platform $1.47, no surge at 1.0×, F7, F6), so per RD-2 the refund is limited to the unexempted segment's extra km × the metered per-km rate: 4.78 km × $1.41/km = $6.74.

The driver's only previous upheld dispute in 90 days was a no-show matter and not a route deviation (F16: 1 upheld, route: 0), so this case is not a 'repeated' route violation and the RD-6 account flag is not engaged.

weaknesses: The GPS record contradicts any 'GPS rerouted me' defence for the second segment: F4 shows a 4.78 km detour up to 1687 m off the optimal route, and F10 is only the driver's own statement, which loses to the system record — the rider will rely on F3/F4 plus F1 (total +8.5 km, +41%) to argue the trip was substantially off-route.
